messages:
jess-support: Heads up — AcmePay (enterprise) opened an escalation: p99 for /v1/generate from eu-west jumped to ~3.2s at ~08:10 UTC. Baseline ~150-250ms. Ticket #12345. They included a quick traceroute showing an extra hop to us-east then back.
ana (oncall): on it. Can you paste the traceroute + a sample request-id? I’ll start a parallel probe from our eu-west probe fleet.
jess-support: traceroute snippet: \n  traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.178.45.10), 8 hops max
   1  10.10.1.1  1.2 ms
   2  edge-eu-west-pop (35.178.45.2)  12 ms
   3  gw-us-east (3.12.34.1)  600 ms
   4  edge-eu-west-pop (35.178.45.2)  600 ms
request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
paul-net: that looks like a hairpin — traffic picked a us-east egress then back to eu-west. Could be GSLB/anycast steering or an active healthcheck flap on the eu-west NLB announcing it as unhealthy.
monitoring-bot: Alert: route-path-inflation detected for backend cluster eu-west-pool-3; p95->p99 delta 2.9s at 08:09:42 UTC. Recent config: net/bgproutes/2026-03-10 applied by paul-net.
paul-net: checking BGP changes now. I see a route withdraw for prefix 35.178.45.0/24 around 08:07 UTC from eu-west POP due to healthprobe failures, then a reannounce from us-east. Investigating probe logs.
ana (oncall): can we repro externally? I'll run curl with timing from eu-west probe.
lee-platform: if this is a GSLB decision, we can pin AcmePay's tenant to eu-west via the tenant-routing override (short-term) and set their route TTL low. That will avoid cross-region selection while we fix the root cause.
ana (oncall): repro command: \n  curl -w 'time_connect:%{time_connect} time_pretransfer:%{time_pretransfer} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer} total:%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d'
  result: time_connect:0.050 time_pretransfer:1.450 time_starttransfer:1.480 total:3.210
jess-support: so TLS handshake (pretransfer) is the big gap — ~1.4s. TCP connect is fine.
paul-net: TLS hang + hairpin smell => likely an anycast/GSLB choice that sends initial SYN to us-east, TLS handshake completes when packet returns to eu-west (extra RTT) and then app-level continues. Looking at NLB healthcheck logs I see a flappy probe because of a failed TLS cert reload on the edge instance in eu-west pool at 08:06.
paul-net: commit id net/bgproutes/2026-03-10 rolled back? Not yet. The healthcheck triggered auto-withdraw of the local route. That caused GSLB to prefer us-east.
lee-platform: mitigation plan (short): 1) restart edge service on eu-west pool to fix cert reload failure (paul-net). 2) bump GSLB healthcheck threshold + extend probe window for 10m to avoid flip-flop (ana). 3) apply tenant-routing override for AcmePay to force eu-west (lee). 4) lower DNS TTL for prefix for 5m so client caches update quickly (jess-support).
paul-net: restarted edge service on eu-west pool-3 at 08:28 UTC. Cert reload error fixed (logs show successful reload). NLB healthchecks resumed passing at 08:29.
monitoring-bot: route-change detected: prefix 35.178.45.0/24 reannounced from eu-west at 08:29:12 UTC. p99 falling.
ana (oncall): applied GSLB probe smoothing (threshold +3 good checks) at 08:30. lee applied tenant override for AcmePay to eu-west at 08:31.
jess-support: lowered DNS TTL for affected prefix to 60s at 08:32, asked AcmePay to flush local resolver (they did). Sent status update to customer.
paul-net: post-mitigation curl from eu-west: time_connect:0.045 time_pretransfer:0.120 time_starttransfer:0.155 total:0.210 — TLS handshake back to normal.
jess-support: AcmePay confirmed p99 back to ~200ms after ~15m. Closing loop with them, will keep monitoring for 2h.
lee-platform: follow-ups: add a CI check around cert reload on edge deploys, and add a guard so healthcheck flapping doesn't withdraw BGP routes until X consecutive failures. Filed followup tickets: INF-2041 (cert-reload CI), NET-1987 (healthcheck hysteresis).
ana (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Leaving monitoring for 2h window. If anything reoccurs, ping @oncall-sre.
jess-support: thanks all. :heart:
